subject: Evaluation runbook handoff + vendor gap analysis — latency & concurrency

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Evaluation runbook handoff + vendor gap analysis — latency & concurrency

Hi Linda / NovaCorp team,

Per our MAP milestone for close, attaching the evaluation runbook and the initial benchmark digest we ran against your sample workload. High level: we measured token TTFT, end-to-end latency, steady-state throughput, and concurrency behavior for the three candidate model variants you asked about. The short summary: average P50 TTFT is within the range we previewed, but we observed tail latency spikes when concurrency > 8 on your request shape.

Actionable next steps I want us to agree on this week:
- Confirm the exact client harness you used for your re-run (tooling, flags, sequence distribution).
- Share a 10-30 min reproducer (single script + small payload) so our infra team can run on an identical instance.
- Book a joint reproduction session (we propose Tue 29 Sep or Wed 30 Sep).

Attachments: nova_map_v1.xlsx (MAP with timeline), nova-tooling-sample-logs.txt (our raw harness logs).

Notes on methodology (short):
- We used continuous batching with dynamic KV cache sizing; target batch window 20ms.
- Input padding and tokenization were applied to match your dataset token length distribution (see sheet "seq-dist").
- We instrumented TTFT at the tokenizer boundary and at final token emit to capture overheads.

If you prefer, I can loop in a dedicated infra engineer for the repro call. Confirm availability and any constraints (on-prem agents, VPN).

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

Jordan — thanks for the handoff and the MAP. We re-ran the suite this morning on our staging cluster and are seeing consistently higher TTFT for the same sample input (P50 ~210ms vs your 160ms; P95 ~520ms vs your 320ms). Concurrency pattern was a stepped load (1, 4, 8, 16) and the degradation shows up when we reach ~8 concurrent callers.

I've attached a short extract of our harness output and the exact run command we used (we used an internal harness derived from kbench, not your provided script). Emptying KV cache between trials didn't materially change the tail.

Can your infra team try to reproduce with our harness? We're available Tue 29 Sep 14:00-16:00 PT. Also: we are running on a cloud VM with NVIDIA A10G and GDS disabled; is that different from your testbed?

Thanks — Linda

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Linda Hughes <linda.hughes@novacorp.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:16:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation runbook handoff + vendor gap analysis — latency & concurrency

Linda / team — thanks for the run data, helpful. A few quick hypotheses and an ask for exact reproducer details so we can triage:

Hypotheses (what commonly causes this mismatch):
- Harness differences: padding/tokenizer behavior, batching window, and client-side request shaping can change observed TTFT by 20-40%.
- Hardware/GPU config: GDS vs non-GDS, MIG slices, or driver versions (we usually test on A100/80GB or A10G with GDS enabled — vendor defaults matter).
- Batch scheduling edge cases under 8+ concurrency: our runtime uses a continuous batching scheduler with a 20ms target; if your harness fires in microbursts it may trigger variable batch sizes and higher tail.
- Quantization/ops parity: if one run uses an INT8 path and the other runs FP16, kernel selection can change latency profiles.

Ask: please share the exact run command, the harness repo commit/tag, and a sample 3–5 request payload file. If you can't share, record the following from your run: --batch-window-ms, --max-batch-size, --prefill-behavior, and driver versions.

Immediate repro plan I propose:
1) Wed 30 Sep 14:00 PT — joint session where NovaCorp shares their harness and we run it on an identical VM image (we'll provision an A10G with GDS toggled per your environment).
2) If mismatch persists, we will toggle scheduling flags (batch window 10/20/40ms) and quantization pathways and record P50/P95/P99 across runs.
3) Post-repro: update MAP with a short remediation checklist (configuration, recommended VM image, and expected delta to close).

I've added a short checklist attachment and a minimal repro command we will run on our side.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 10:03:32 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation runbook handoff + vendor gap analysis — latency & concurrency

Hi all — following the Wed session we ran a mirrored suite and compiled a short CSV summarizing the differences (attached: nova-benchmark-summary-20261001.csv). TL;DR: when we ran Nova's harness exactly (same command and payload) on our A10G image with GDS disabled we could reproduce the higher P95 but only when the client sent variable-length microbursts (bursts of 1-3 requests every 10ms). With a steady poisson traffic shape the numbers align closer to our original runs.

Competitive note: we also ran a quick head-to-head against CompetitorX's hosted offering using the same harness. CompetitorX showed similar tail behavior under microbursts but had slightly better batching smoothing at 16 concurrency (likely due to a fixed-window batcher baked into their stack). This is captured in the CSV (columns: env, concurrency, p50, p95, p99, batch-median-size).

Updated MAP items:
- Repro window: joint tuning session to settle on batch window and batching policy (owner: Karthik).
- Config recommendation: A10G image + driver v525.60, GDS disabled for parity (owner: NovaCorp infra).
- Expected delta: median TTFT improvement ~25% when shifting from microburst to steady traffic or when batch windows are increased to 30-40ms.
- Close target: finalize config and sign-off by 2026-10-14 to hit renewal/commit cadence.

Ben and I can prepare a short one-pager for your procurement team that calls out expected unit economics deltas once the MAP is applied.

Best — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Linda — thanks for the fast turnaround and for joining the repro session. Quick summary + action items to keep the MAP and close timeline moving:

Summary:
- Root cause appears to be request shaping (microbursts) interacting with a continuous batching scheduler; parity achieved when either (a) client smooths traffic to steady poisson, or (b) batch window is increased to 30–40ms.
- NovaCorp agrees to test the recommended A10G image + driver v525.60 with GDS disabled this week.
- We captured competitive comparison notes vs CompetitorX in the attached runbook and CSV; helpful context but does not materially change config steps.

Action items (owners & dates):
- NovaCorp infra: run config test on prod-like staging image and report P50/P95 by 2026-10-11 (owner: Linda).
- Redwood infra: prepare a short runbook and procurement-facing one-pager with estimated token economics impact (owner: Ben) by 2026-10-12.
- Karthik: finalize recommended batch-window defaults and a fallback policy for microburst detection by 2026-10-10.
- Jordan/Marissa: prepare final MAP update with sign-off section for procurement (owner: Jordan) by 2026-10-14.

If everyone confirms those owners/dates I will update HubSpot (DEAL-7092) and move the close milestone accordingly. Please reply with a quick thumbs-up or any changes.

Thanks — Jordan
